title: Tests, Grades and Learning at Home
text:
Many students feel that tests measure their worth, yet a single exam rarely shows the full extent of what they have learned. Grades can motivate some learners, but they can also make others anxious and reluctant to take risks in class. For this reason, teachers increasingly combine formal assessments with projects and regular feedback.

Learning at home plays an important role in this process. Parents who ask questions about daily lessons, rather than only asking about marks, help children see mistakes as part of learning. Consequently, students often become more confident and more willing to try difficult tasks, even when the results are not perfect.

questions.text: According to paragraph one, what can grades do to some learners?
options: They can make learners anxious and reluctant to take risks
They remove the need for homework

questions.text: According to paragraph two, what do parents do that helps children see mistakes as part of learning?
options: They forbid children from making mistakes
They ask questions about daily lessons

questions.text: What does the passage suggest about relying on a single exam?
options: It gives a complete picture of a student's ability
It may not fully reflect what a student has learned
It is the best way to motivate every learner
It is preferred by parents over projects

questions.text: Why might students who learn at home with supportive parents become more willing to try difficult tasks?
options: Because they fear losing their grades
Because they no longer need to study
Because they see errors as a normal step in learning
Because difficult tasks are removed from the curriculum

vocabulary.definition: formal tests or methods used to judge how much someone has learned
worried and nervous about something that may happen
information given to someone about how well they are doing

paragraph_translations: Muitos alunos sentem que as provas medem o seu valor, mas uma única avaliação raramente mostra toda a extensão do que aprenderam. As notas podem motivar alguns estudantes, mas também podem deixar outros ansiosos e relutantes em correr riscos na sala de aula. Por essa razão, os professores combinam cada vez mais avaliações formais com projetos e feedback regular.

A aprendizagem em casa desempenha um papel importante nesse processo. Pais que fazem perguntas sobre as aulas do dia a dia, em vez de perguntar apenas sobre as notas, ajudam as crianças a ver os erros como parte da aprendizagem. Consequentemente, os alunos costumam ficar mais confiantes e mais dispostos a tentar tarefas difíceis, mesmo quando os resultados não são perfeitos.
